Black Friday 2026: These unexpected items are driving up U.S. consumer spending

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1653 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fastcompany

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • retail industry’s version of the Super Bowl is here with the arrival of Black Friday, an occasion that sellers online and in stores seize to drive year-end sales.
  • retail industry’s version of the Super Bowl is here with the arrival of Black Friday, an occasion that sellers online and in stores seize to drive year-end sales.
  • This year’s holiday shopping takes place in a U.S.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the U.S. retail industry’s version of the Super Bowl is here with the arrival of Black Friday, an occasion that sellers online and in stores seize to drive year-end sales. This year, the day once considered the holiday shopping season’s unofficial kickoff might look to spectators more like the fourth quarter of a football game.Brands and retailers have promoted steep discounts under the Black Friday banner all month, and some began rolling out deals before Halloween. But enough die-hard traditionalists hit the shops as soon as they can after Thanksgiving that the day remains the year’s biggest for foot traffic at physical stores, according to Sensormatic Solutions, a retail technology company.“Black Friday is still the day for in-store shopping,” noted Grant Gustafson, Sensormatic’s head of retail consulting and analytics.Stores also have kept drawing a majority of holiday season spending, although e-commerce captures a bigger share every year, according to U.S. Census data. Industry analysts expect the trend to continue; consumers spent $82.5 billion online from November 1 to November 22, a 9.1% increase from the comparable three weeks last year, according to research by Adobe.Retailers and consumers are giving Black Friday 2026 some other twists. The day’s evolution into a multiweek event has encouraged shoppers to stock up on discounted household basics while checking off their holiday lists, retail analysts said. Artificial intelligence and cost concerns are influencing how, where, when and on what consumers spend, retail analysts said.“It’s not just a moment where shoppers are buying gifts,” said Caila Schwartz, a retail and consumer insights leader at Salesforce. “They’re also buying things that they need, and so that’s going to help drive up a lot of the spend.”Here’s more on the emerging trends for Black Friday and holiday shopping overall: Low views of the economy aren’t expected to dim holiday sales This year’s holiday shopping takes place in a U.S. economic environment marked by voter frustration over gasoline prices fueled by the U.S. war with Iran, and high inflation overall.Analysts and economists scrutinize retail spending on the five days that begin with Thanksgiving Day and end on Cyber Monday for clues about consumers’ financial staying power and commercial prospects heading into the new year.Retail sales were up and down all year as filling up a car and other nonnegotiable costs took more out of household budgets. Commerce Department figures for October showed Americans pulling back on buying books, clothes, sporting goods, and other items.The good news for retailers is that consumer confidence jumped this month as U.S. gas prices continued a steady decline.The National Retail Federation estimated that higher prices would account for about half of the 4.1% sales growth it expected in stores and online in November and December. The group forecast U.S. shoppers collectively spending $1.01 trillion. Black Friday still might have bigger discounts despite early deals U.S. retailers have broadly held the line on prices instead of making big increases across the board, and offered solid discounts that persuaded customers to shop earlier, industry analysts said.Salesforce, which tracks digital spending at a range of retailers, including grocery stores, said November discounts before Black Friday were 8% bigger than last year’s. Early promotions pushed average selling prices of physical merchandise 1% below last November’s prices, Salesforce said.Retailers nonetheless were likely to reserve their best prices for Thanksgiving Day and Black Friday, Vivek Pandya, director of digital insights at Adobe, said.For example, discounts on TVs are expected to average 23% on Friday compared with 11% during the first 22 days of the month, according to Adobe. Shoppers are buying household items along with holiday gifts The deepest discounts between this past Tuesday and Monday were expected on clothing, home goods, and health and beauty, Salesforce said. The company said it expected health and beauty products to average 33% off.With Black Friday commencing well before the day itself, some consumers apply seasonal bargains to last long after the holidays by filling their cupboards with toiletries and clothes they would typically buy at another time, according to analysts.Online sales of personal hygiene products were 40% higher from November 1 through November 22 compared with the October average, according to Adobe’s data. Sales of household cleaning products spiked 33% and clothing basics by 27% during the same time frame, Adobe said.“Usually, when you think of holiday shopping, it’s premium handbags and jewelry and those types of items, but we’re fast seeing shoppers also use this season to stock up on the essentials,” Pandya said. AI tools may be persuading users to do more online shopping Consumers are using AI-powered shopping tools to help them compare products and prices, particularly as inflation and paying more for gasoline have made them more attuned to price tags, Pandya said.Traffic to online retail sites from links in AI-powered tools more than doubled this month compared with November 2025, Adobe said.A belief that e-commerce sites will offer “the best value possible” has contributed to shoppers’ doing more of their holiday period spending online instead of in stores, Pandya said. —Anne D’Innocenzio, AP Retail Writer.

‘It was the talk of the playground’: Google’s AI features blocked by L.A. school officials

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2363 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fastcompany

⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • School districts are taking steps to block Google’s artificial intelligence features and are considering dropping Google products entirely unless the company gives them a permanent AI workaround, pitting them against the tech giant whose Chromebook computers and learning tools are deeply embedded in America’s classrooms.In a major step, Los Angeles school officials have quietly disabled AI-generated summaries, known as AI Overview, in Google searches on school-issued devices.
  • It has been revealed that school districts are taking steps to block Google’s artificial intelligence features and are considering dropping Google products entirely unless the organization gives them a permanent AI workaround, pitting them against the tech giant whose Chromebook computers and learning tools are deeply embedded in America’s classrooms.In a major step, Los Angeles school officials have quietly disabled AI-generated summaries, known as AI Overview, in Google searches on school-issued devices.
  • Sources indicate that schools are seeing growing backlash against technology, starting with cell phones and screen time and now focusing on AI, amid concerns that students are using AI to think for them.The Mountain View, California-based company in August found itself at the center of controversy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

School districts are taking steps to block Google’s artificial intelligence features and are considering dropping Google products entirely unless the company gives them a permanent AI workaround, pitting them against the tech giant whose Chromebook computers and learning tools are deeply embedded in America’s classrooms.In a major step, Los Angeles school officials have quietly disabled AI-generated summaries, known as AI Overview, in Google searches on school-issued devices. The move makes the Los Angeles Unified School District (LAUSD) the largest district to sideline the company, which has stated it will not separate its search product from AI tools for education.The L.A. district, which enrolls half a million students, has made no formal announcement, and the move caught parents and students by surprise, said Bridie Lee, a leader of Schools Beyond Screens LA, which has pushed for screen-time limits and tech oversight in the district.The group had several members who weighed in at a meeting of the Los Angeles school board’s AI committee on Friday, November 13. By that Monday, AI Overview was gone.“It was the talk of the playground,” Lee said.Google is the dominant provider of education technology for America’s classrooms. Beyond its low-cost Chromebooks, the most widely used student laptops, Google’s suite of education apps like Google Docs and Classroom has become integral to classwork, homework, and communication among students and teachers.But concerns about AI’s impact on learning have ignited a battle between schools and Google. In September, the country’s two largest school districts—in New York and L.A.—announced one-year moratoriums on student use of generative AI, and Google has said it’s not possible to take AI out of its search products. Schools are considering other internet search providers.LAUSD said in a statement it temporarily suspended AI Overview to ensure student experiences are “age-appropriate and safe.” It also said it continually evaluates its digital safeguards, including third-party tools. It was likely using such a tool that it was able to disable AI Overview.Schools Beyond Screens LA asked parents to send videos of what laptop screens looked like and received clips showing that AI Overview was no longer an option in Google search on district devices. Then activists reached out to the district, which confirmed AI Overview was disabled. Lee said they had no other details on how it was done or how long it is intended to stay disabled.“We’re thrilled LAUSD did this,” said Lee. “AI is seeping into everything. It’s dangerous. It’s hurting learning. And it’s a corporate overreach into public schools. It’s Big Tech attempting to strongarm tech policy without anyone’s consent.”Other districts, such as Fairfax County Public Schools in Virginia, have developed plug-ins to remove AI summaries for students searching on Google, according to multiple published reports. Google is increasingly at center of school tech backlash Schools are seeing growing backlash against technology, starting with cell phones and screen time and now focusing on AI, amid concerns that students are using AI to think for them.The Mountain View, California-based company in August found itself at the center of controversy. That’s when it said it had turned on its Gemini chatbot for many K-12 students using Google Classroom, its learning management system. Weeks later, New York City and L.A. schools banned generative AI. In New York, the ban applies to all elementary and middle school students, and in Los Angeles all students K-12 are banned from using AI on school devices. Both districts said the ban would allow officials to develop AI policies this academic year.Then, in early November, Google backtracked. It published a blog post saying it would instead turn off Gemini and all search tools by default for K-12 schools in the coming months. Administrators would have to turn on each tool if they wanted students to access them.Google said this was to give schools more choice. But the choice to turn off AI altogether is not there.While the blog post does not explicitly say search can’t be used without AI, Chris Phillips, vice president for education at Google, told The New York Times: “Search and AI are deeply integrated.” If schools ban AI, students “will not have access to search, and they’ll see a message from their school that indicates it’s not available.”The integration of AI in search isn’t new. Google introduced AI Overview in 2025, and anyone who uses Google search will get AI answers to many search results. Google insists AI Overview is an integral part of its search product now and cannot be separated.Earlier this month, hundreds of Google employees signed a petition asking the company’s leadership to allow schools to turn off AI features “without disrupting their ability to use search as a whole.”“The way the decision has been reported in the press is poor, and makes Google, and our Education and Search products as a result, look like we’re punishing schools for not using AI,” the petition said. “Many students, educators and parents have concerns about AI in the classroom, as is shown by many school districts who have placed moratoriums or bans on such technology. It is our job as Googlers to respect the user, and listen to them when they have concerns about our products.” Google has made some changes—but not enough, activists say Google says it hears parents’ and teachers’ concerns about students using AI to “shortcut learning” and that it shares the same goal: helping students learn. But what many parents and teachers want—the ability to bypass AI entirely and allow students to use Google search like it was in, say, 2024—is not something Google offers. This has forced districts across the U.S. to choose between restricting students’ access to AI and maintaining access to the popular search engine.Instead of offering an AI-free search product for schools, Google announced a pilot “guided learning” tool that walks students “step-by-step through a range of complex problems, instead of just giving quick answers.”“We are actively building these experiences in partnership with educators, listening closely to ensure our products support students and teachers,” the company said in a statement.Presently, Google search offers AI Overview, which contains summarized answers resulting from general searches, and AI Mode, which is a chatbot interaction. Guided learning, which is not yet available, will walk users through steps intended to support critical thinking to get to the answer.L.A. schools had already disabled Google’s AI Mode at the beginning of the school year on school-issued student devices, said Jack Kelanic, the district’s chief information officer, during a school board committee meeting on artificial intelligence last week. Educators and staff still have access.“We understand this as a deeper embedding of AI into the education suite,” Kelanic said. He added, to applause, that the district is not bound to Google’s products if officials determine the changes are not in line with the district’s priorities.“We have choices,” Kelanic said. “We can change the default search engine literally overnight.” The Associated Press’ education coverage receives financial support from multiple private foundations. Use the recorded vocal as the timing reference. AI tools can help build opening shots, instrumental cutaways, and singing performances. Compare MakeSong, HeyGen, and Hedra on the singing shots themselves, and try Freebeat for an audio-led visual draft.

AISong provides an image-led way to build the visual world around a recorded track. It fits a performance video that uses atmosphere and supporting shots in addition to views of the singer.

AISong’s AI Music Video Generator combines the song with a set of image references for a multi-shot sequence. Use that feature for the opening, an instrumental cutaway, or an establishing scene that can support the performance footage. Check whether the setting and the singer’s close-up look like they belong in the same video.

Sources indicate that when preparing these assets for a website or multimedia project, consistency between images and video clips is crucial. This is also relevant to the process of building an AI media pipeline from concept art to web video.

Portrait art, rehearsal stills, or images of the setting can give these supporting shots an established look. It is particularly useful when some parts of the song call for visuals that give the audience a break from the performer.

In a recent development, makeSong can build a video around the recorded track and reference images. Its lip-sync option requires a real human face. Start with a clear frontal image and check the result against the original vocal.

Sources indicate that makeSong’s AI Music Video Generator accepts audio, images, and a written prompt. The product page also offers lip sync for eligible face references. Give the close-up a particular vocal phrase and reserve a wider shot for the next musical response. Check mouth timing and the performer’s appearance at the cut.

This approach works when a single visual brief needs to connect the performance with the supporting scenes. The artist should have an approved reference and a clear idea of when the singer should appear.

In a recent development, heyGen is a performer-led music video option. It is particularly relevant when the same on-screen singer should remain recognizable through more than one setting or camera distance.

Its music video workflow accepts a song and supports singing performance. Use a close and a wider view to compare mouth timing and continuity on the same vocal phrase. Watch for changes in the face or outfit when the framing shifts.

Choose this route when viewers need to follow the same singer across several scenes. This makes more sense than a single avatar clip when the performer is the visual thread for the whole video.

Hedra can animate a portrait from an audio clip. Try a single line with a quick consonant followed by a held vowel to see where the mouth falls behind the recording.

According to recent reports, A clear portrait and one clean line give you a controlled test. Inspect the start and end of the phrase, then check how the clip cuts to the next shot. When only one line is convincing, use that line and let the original edit carry the rest.

A short close-up or a fictional singer’s entrance in the chorus is a good use for this approach. It is a practical fit when you already have an edit and only need one additional vocal moment.

Freebeat offers an audio-to-video workflow with a performance-oriented mode. It gives artists another way to test a performance cut driven by an uploaded track.

Use its singing video route for an excerpt with an audible pause and a clear vocal re-entry. Compare whether the performance feels natural during the pause and whether the visual action resumes where the vocal does. Keep the same approved track for the comparison.

Try this early to compare a full performance treatment with a version built from shorter clips before settling on an edit.

Breaking: Travis and Jason Kelce’s Garage Beer lands $20 million as craft brewers pull back

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that travis Kelce’s beer brand just secured a huge financial deal to help promote its popular brew.
  • Industry observers note that travis Kelce’s beer brand just secured a huge financial deal to help promote its popular brew.
  • Industry observers note that the funding comes at a time when the independent beer industry has been facing many challenges.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that travis Kelce’s beer brand just secured a huge financial deal to help promote its popular brew. On Tuesday, Travis and his brother Jason Kelce’s Garage Beer brand secured a $20 million revolving credit from Tiger Finance, according to a release. The funding comes at a time when the independent beer industry has been facing many challenges. The rise in operation costs, slowing business openings, and declines in sales have forced many breweries to close down or refinance. But this celebrity-backed brand is only seeing success. Andy Cerussi, the senior managing director of Tiger Finance, noted in the release that the manufacturer is thrilled to have been chosen as the preferred financial partner, saying that the company is “impressed with [the] impact the Kelce brothers have had on positively influencing brand awareness.” Brian Amicon, president of Garage Beer, told Inc. that as the company continues to grow, this financing allows it greater flexibility. “From strengthening our distribution to investing in the brand and creating more opportunities to connect with consumers, it puts us in a strong position to keep building what we’ve started,” Amicon said. “We’re proud of the progress we’ve made and excited to keep pushing forward.” A $20 million bet on Garage Beer’s brand strength The debt deal allows Garage Beer to expand its product line and enter latest markets. At $20 million, the financing sits on the smaller side of the funding spectrum—in the bottom quarter of deals tracked, according to Deal Room. But for a consumer company like a beer line, debt against brand strength gives growth capital without diluting equity. This revolving line will give Garage Beer flexible access to capital tied to its brand value. The Columbus, Ohio-based brand originally introduced as a local craft light lager by Braxton Brewing Co., but was spun off into an independent company in 2023 by its CEO, Andy Sauer. According to VinePair, the Kelce brothers joined Garage Beer in the summer of 2024 by acquiring a majority stake and becoming co-owners and operators. This move rapidly boosted the brand’s national visibility. In late 2025, Durational Capital Management announced its strategic investment partnership with the company. A cofounder of Durational Capital said in the release that the company appreciates Tiger’s creativity and partnership “to structure a credit facility that leverages the strength of Garage Beer’s brand to support the company’s growth objectives.” Garage Beer is expanding while competitors retrench Neil Reid, a professor at the University of Toledo who studies the craft beer industry, told Inc. that the brand’s trajectory stands out. “Garage Beer’s aggressive expansion is highly unusual in today’s beer market,” Reid said. He noted that the company has expanded distribution to all 50 states and added more than 100,000 barrels of volume in 2025, reportedly the largest increase among U.S. craft brewers. “Rather than retrenching, Garage Beer is using the downturn to gain market share from competitors,” Reid told Inc. He added that brands with the capacity for growth through distribution often tend to be a simple product and have broad appeal, sales momentum, enough capital to fund expansion, name recognition, and scalable operations. Brands like small craft breweries that rely on taprooms and direct sales struggle with reaching that same momentum. Even if they have strong local followings, having fewer financial resources and less distributor support can be a challenge. “By offering a simple, familiar product rather than a niche craft beer, the brand can attract a larger audience, generate stronger retail turnover, and expand more easily across geographic markets,” Reid said. But he cautioned against treating Garage Beer as a model for the rest of the industry, noting, “The brand benefits from factors that most breweries lack, including celebrity backing, substantial capital, extensive marketing reach, and a highly scalable business model. Differentiation remains vital, but differentiation alone is rarely sufficient.” Celebrity attention still has to translate into repeat sales Claudia Kubowicz Malhotra, marketing professor at the University of North Carolina’s Kenan-Flagler Business School, told Inc. that celebrity attention is only the first step. “To continue to build the brand, awareness needs to translate to interest, desire, and action,” Kubowicz Malhotra said. “Consumers need to look and ask for the beer by name. Ultimately, this needs to translate to sales.” As Garage Beer adds new products, she said, it can grow successfully “if new product offerings reinforce the brand positioning—a light beer that tastes like beer.” To judge whether the brand has staying power, Kubowicz Malhotra told Inc. she would look beyond sales: “I would also look for customer retention and repurchase behavior as well as word of mouth.” Tiger Finance and Durational Capital Management did not immediately respond to Inc.’s request for comment. —Lucia Auerbach This article originally appeared on Fast Company’s sister website, Inc.com. Getting a gaming laptop this Black Friday doesn't have to be a hassle. In case you're after the best deals that we've found thus far across a range of configurations, in addition to explanations of why these models in particular should be on your radar. Getting a gaming laptop is pretty tough — different systems can tout similar specs, but in reality, their performance can vary wildly. This is down to different power ratings across mobile GPUs, which can muddy the waters when you're looking on storefronts. It's often obfuscated in listings or omitted entirely.

The Asus ROG Strix G16 comes with a 16-inch screen, with an 1900 x 1200 pixel resolution, a 16:10 aspect ratio, and refresh and response rates of 165Hz and 3ms, respectively. Hardware inside this gaming laptop includes Nvidia's GeForce RTX 5070 Ti laptop GPU, an AMD Ryzen 9 8940HX processor, 16GB of DDR5 RAM, and a 1TB SSD for storage.

According to recent reports, this Asus ROG Strix G16 gaming laptop offers a solid price-to-performance ratio and comes with AMD's Ryzen 9 8940HX CPU, sporting 16 cores and 32 threads. Packing in the gaming punch is the included RTX 5070 Ti 12GB, with GDDR7 memory and a total graphics power of 115W; this is the full-fat variant of the chip, and dynamic boost can also see this rise to up to 140W. When paired with a relatively modest screen resolution and display, it certainly bodes well for getting solid performance from modern titles. And you should be able to saturate the display's refresh rate when turning on features like Multi Frame Generation in single-player titles.

One thing to keep in mind here is that the laptop does sacrifice display quality, and its CPU isn't on the latest Zen 5 architecture; it's based on AMD's Zen 4 Dragon Range refresh chips. But it's still mighty fast and should suit both gaming and productivity workloads.

Get a 16-inch gaming laptop with Intel Core Ultra 7 255HX, RTX 5070 Ti with 12GB of VRAM, 16GB of DDR5 RAM, and a 512GB SSD.

Coming in slightly cheaper than the above Asus ROG Strix system, this MSI Vector 16 HX AI laptop from Newegg offers much of the same specifications: right down to the TGP of the GPU. MSI's 5070 Ti mobile chip carries the same 115W TGP, in addition to the screen resolution. It also moves CPUs to Intel's 20-core, 20-thread Core Ultra 7 255HX, which is a newer architecture compared to the ROG Strix G16's Dragon Range offering. However, you get a lower screen refresh rate at 144Hz and half the storage included. It does trade blows effectively with the Asus model in many respects, though, including offering dual Thunderbolt 5 ports and a 2.5GbE port over the ROG Strix's 1GbE port. With the sizes of modern games, though, it's tough to outright tell you to run out and purchase a system with only 512 GB of storage, so this system remains our alternative pick for most people.

The MSI Crosshair sports a 16-inch, 240Hz display with a 2560 x 1600 resolution that's powered by an 115W max TGP Nvidia RTX 5060 graphics with 8GB of GDDR7 VRAM. Other specs include an AMD Ryzen 7 8840HX processor, 16GB of memory, and a 1TB SSD.

According to recent reports, this MSI Crosshair 16 deal at Walmart sports a tricked-out 115W RTX 5060 GPU at its core, alongside a 12-core, 24-thread AMD Ryzen 7 8840HX Dragon Range CPU that can boost up to 5.1GHz. Sporting 1TB of NVMe storage and 16GB of DDR5 RAM, this more entry-level system can offer solid computing power while staying within a limited budget. Something that prospective buyers should watch out for is the display's resolution: you get a 16:10, 2560 x 1600 screen resolution and 240Hz refresh rate on this system, meaning that the laptop will likely struggle in modern titles, especially at high settings. Turning on upscaling tech like DLSS might help smooth things over somewhat, but given that you'll be doing things other than gaming on this laptop, it makes for a comfortable everyday system that offers a sharp display.

Lenovo's Legion 5i sports a 15.3-inch, 3K display that's powered by an Intel Core 7 245HX processor, an Nvidia GeForce RTX 5060 graphics card, and 16GB of RAM. For storage, there's a 512GB SSD.

Our alternative budget pick here is the Lenovo Legion 5i gaming laptop, which is discounted by $700 at Best Buy. You get the same 115W RTX 5060 silicon as the MSI model above, but with an Intel Core 7 245HX, with 14 cores and 14 threads and a boost clock of up to 5.1GHz on the P-cores. You also get the same 16:10 aspect ratio and 2560 x 1600 resolution, but on a 165Hz OLED panel. If you care about getting the best contrast ratios and response time, this might be the pick for you, as saturating a 240Hz display with an RTX 5060 mobile variant will be a pretty tall task. However, this comes with the downside that you once again sacrifice the amount of storage available on the system here, with only 512GB available here.

Get an HP Omen Max laptop with an RTX 5080 GPU, Ryzen 9 HX 375, a 1TB SSD, and 32GB of RAM, all packed into a 16-inch chassis with a 2560 x 1600 240Hz display.

It has been revealed that if you're looking to spend in the high-end, then this RTX 5080-based system with a full-fat wattage of up to 175W (under dynamic boost), paired with an AMD Ryzen AI 9 HX 375, which offers 12 cores and 24 threads, with a max boost clock of up to 5.1GHz should be able to chew up most workloads you throw its way. The 2560 x 1600, 240Hz display makes much more sense here, and with full VRR support and 32GB of DDR5 in tow, this is a bona fide powerhouse, and you'll pay for the privilege at almost $3,000. With that said, you get 1TB of storage here, which is slightly disappointing, but given how NAND pricing is going, it's par for the course right now.

The hardware included inside the Gigabyte Gaming A16 Pro includes Nvidia's RTX 5080 laptop graphics card with 16GB of VRAM, an Intel Core 7 240H processor, 32GB of RAM, and a 1TB SSD.

Recent findings suggest that coming in at just over $2,000, the Gigabyte Gaming A16 Pro deal at Walmart offers a 10-core, 16-thread Core Ultra 7 240H CPU and an RTX 5080 GPU with 16GB of GDDR7 VRAM. The difference between the Omen 16 Max and this Gigabyte model is that this particular RTX 5080 has a lower TGP of 115W, but maintains the same amount of VRAM. In real-world terms, your framerates will undoubtedly be slower, and saturating its 16-inch, 2560 x 1600 display will be a lot more difficult. However, that neutered power limit also puts it in contention with the RTX 5070 Ti-based systems we've listed, but with more VRAM. If that 4GB difference matters to you, and you are willing to pay the difference, then this deal offers a solid amount of silicon for your cash.

Get an HP Omen Max laptop with an RTX 5090 GPU, a Core Ultra 9 290HX Plus CPU, a 2TB SSD, and 32GB of RAM, all packed into a 16-inch chassis with a 2560 x 1600 240Hz OLED display.

If you're gunning for a gaming behemoth this Black Friday, this desktop-replacement-grade system is worth a look. Sporting an RTX 5090 GPU with 24GB of GDDR7 memory, paired with Intel's Core Ultra 290 HX Plus, with a total of 24 cores and 24 threads (8 P-Cores, 16 E-Cores), and a boost clock of up to 5.5GHz, this monstrous system is paired with 32GB of DDR5-6400 memory and 2TB of PCIe Gen 5 storage. You're also flush with connectivity options, including Wi-Fi 7 support, a pair of Thunderbolt 4 ports, and 2.5GB Ethernet. You also get a rapid 240Hz OLED display that gets plenty bright to boot. If you're spending north of $3,000 on a laptop, this should be it.

Sources indicate that get a great deal on this flagship-class ROG Strix Scar 16 gaming laptop from Amazon. You get the Core Ultra 9 275HX 8p/16e (24 threads) processor, 32GB dual-channel DDR5-5600 RAM, 2TB M.2 PCIe 4.0 x4 NVMe SSD, a 16-inch Mini-LED display (2560x1600) with a fast 240 Hz refresh rate, and the pièce de résistance: a dedicated RTX 5090 24GB laptop GPU. You'll be able to play most games at high frame rates or even run your own local AI models.

At MSRP pricing, the ROG Strix Scar is a better buy every other day. But given that it's black friday, the value offered by the HP Omen Max 16 slightly edges out this equally performant ROG Strix Scar 16 deal at Newegg. Expect the same RTX 5090 laptop GPU with 24GB of GDDR7 memory, but swap in an Intel Core Ultra 275HX with a total of 24 cores and 24 threads with 8 P-Cores and 16 E-Cores with boost clocks of up to 5.4GHz. Additionally, this system offers slower DDR5-5600 memory and slower storage, running at PCIe 4.0 speeds. However, you do get dual Thunderbolt 5 ports, here, and a matte finish on the display. It's still an incredible laptop by all rights, however HP's option edges things out on value, and spec-wise.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Southwest Airlines is taking a slightly different approach to Black Friday this year.
  • Industry observers note that southwest Airlines is taking a slightly different approach to Black Friday this year.
  • On Friday, Southwest announced a three-day promotion that allows Rapid Rewards members to earn a temporary Companion Pass by booking and completing just one round-trip flight or two one-way flights.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Southwest Airlines is taking a slightly different approach to Black Friday this year. Rather than simply discounting flights, the airline is giving travelers an opportunity to earn one of its most coveted perks: the Companion Pass. On Friday, Southwest declared a three-day promotion that allows Rapid Rewards members to earn a temporary Companion Pass by booking and completing just one round-trip flight or two one-way flights. The offer comes just weeks before Southwest is set to overhaul its Rapid Rewards loyalty program, significantly changing how travelers qualify for the benefit. How to earn Southwest’s promotional Companion Pass If you’re already planning to fly over the holidays, earning the pass could be relatively easy. To take advantage of the promotion, travelers will need to: Register for the promotion through Southwest. Book eligible flights between November 27 and November 29. Complete either a single round-trip flight or two one-way flights between November 27 and January 5, 2027. Travelers who score the pass will be able to bring a designated companion on eligible flights between January 8 and March 3, 2027 for free, with the exception of taxes and fees, which start at $5.60 each way. There’s also no limit to the number of eligible flights travelers can use the pass for during the promotional period, so you and your companion could, in theory, go on a 2-month adventure only paying for one of your flights. Southwest is changing how travelers earn a Companion Pass The promotion comes at an interesting time for Southwest. In October, the airline unveiled changes to its Rapid Rewards loyalty program that will take effect on January 1, 2027. Under the existing program, travelers can earn a Companion Pass by completing 100 qualifying one-way flights or accumulating 135,000 Companion Pass qualifying points in a calendar year. Starting in January, Southwest will eliminate Companion Pass qualifying points and instead use Tier Qualifying Points to determine eligibility for elite status and Companion Pass benefits. The airline is also introducing a new milestone reward that gives members three Companion Pass trips, while travelers who reach its new Platinum elite status will receive unlimited companion trips. One of the biggest changes is how credit card rewards factor into the equation. Historically, Southwest credit card welcome bonuses have offered a particularly lucrative shortcut to earning a Companion Pass. Starting in 2027, those bonuses will no longer count toward qualification. The same goes for referral bonuses, anniversary points, and points earned through hotel and rental car partners. Everyday spending on Southwest credit cards will still help travelers qualify, with cardholders earning one Tier Qualifying Point per dollar spent. There’s still time to earn a Companion Pass under the old rules Southwest is giving prospective credit card customers one final opportunity to take advantage of the existing qualification structure. Travelers who apply for a Southwest Rapid Rewards credit card by December 14, are approved, and meet the spending requirements for its welcome bonus can still have those bonus points count toward earning a Companion Pass under the 2026 rules, even if they complete the spending requirement in early 2027. Those who meet the overall qualification requirements can enjoy unlimited companion flights through December 31, 2027. For travelers who don’t fly Southwest often enough to qualify for the traditional Companion Pass, however, this weekend’s Black Friday promotion offers a much easier way to experience the perk, even if only for a couple of months.

There’s also no limit to the number of eligible flights travelers can use the pass for during the promotional period, so you and your companion could, in theory, go on a 2-month adventure only paying for one of your flights.

The promotion comes at an interesting time for Southwest. In October, the airline unveiled changes to its Rapid Rewards loyalty program that will take effect on January 1, 2027.

Under the existing program, travelers can earn a Companion Pass by completing 100 qualifying one-way flights or accumulating 135,000 Companion Pass qualifying points in a calendar year.

Starting in January, Southwest will eliminate Companion Pass qualifying points and instead use Tier Qualifying Points to determine eligibility for elite status and Companion Pass benefits.

The airline is also introducing a upcoming milestone reward that gives members three Companion Pass trips, while travelers who reach its new Platinum elite status will receive unlimited companion trips.

One of the biggest changes is how credit card rewards factor into the equation.

Historically, Southwest credit card welcome bonuses have offered a particularly lucrative shortcut to earning a Companion Pass. Starting in 2027, those bonuses will no longer count toward qualification. The same goes for referral bonuses, anniversary points, and points earned through hotel and rental car partners.

Everyday spending on Southwest credit cards will still help travelers qualify, with cardholders earning one Tier Qualifying Point per dollar spent.

Southwest is giving prospective credit card customers one final opportunity to take advantage of the existing qualification structure.

Travelers who apply for a Southwest Rapid Rewards credit card by December 14, are approved, and meet the spending requirements for its welcome bonus can still have those bonus points count toward earning a Companion Pass under the 2026 rules, even if they complete the spending requirement in early 2027.

Those who meet the overall qualification requirements can enjoy unlimited companion flights through December 31, 2027.

For travelers who don’t fly Southwest often enough to qualify for the traditional Companion Pass, however, this weekend’s Black Friday promotion offers a much easier way to experience the perk, even if only for a couple of months.

These directions show you routes away from roads where two-wheelers aren’t allowed. You may be directed towards shortcuts along narrower side roads.

Sources indicate that the page also explains that it is only available for mobile devices, with no mention of Android Auto and CarPlay. Yet, a number of users are seeing the adjustment on their devices within the past two weeks, so it seems Google is expanding it out to Android Auto. According to recent reports, the people at Sony don’t use words like “product” or “reboot” when they talk about Aibo, the Japanese electronics and entertainment company’s robotic dog.Aibo robots, which first went on sale in 1999, are all sold out and no longer in production. But some owners who had to part with their Aibo have donated the robots to Tokyo-based Sony Group Corp. for an “adoption program,” where they get treated to repairs and upgrades.Those robot pets now have new homes in hospitals and other facilities, bringing solace and smiles to patients and staff.Sony does not disclose the pricing or the number of Aibo robots that have been sold.Packed with sensors, digital cameras and an intelligence of sorts, Aibo has been programmed to remember its name, the owner’s face and its surroundings — details of everyday life that make for a disarming illusion of a personality.The robot barks, cocks its head, moves its ears, waddles toward you, acts happy when petted and goes to “sleep” — in short it simulates a puppy, except this one can take snapshots and monitors its own mechanical dysfunctions.“The owners feel as though they are sending off what has become to them like their own child,” said Sony official Yoshiyuki Katsuno, who oversees the program.Aibo gets people talking to each other, and can offer tired souls a perk to pick themselves up and keep going, according to Katsuno.“We hope to spread the emotional healing and human interaction that Aibo has to offer,” he said.At the St. Marianna University School of Medicine in Kawasaki, on the outskirts of Tokyo, a nurse had to do some looking to find a wandering Aibo during a recent visit.But Aibo has helped with the long waits for visiting patients and succeeded in persuading reluctant children to get examined, claims Dr. Manabu Komori of the department of otolaryngology.That field involves diagnosing and treating sicknesses related to the ear, nose and throat, with many child patients.“It helps motivate the kids,” Komori said. “Going to a hospital is basically not very pleasant.”The hospital also uses real dogs to help patients feel better, though the animals require care and food and can be temperamental. That means a robot dog offers some advantages, although Komori was careful not to say they were better than real dogs.Cuteness is seen as desirable in Japanese culture, where being “kawaii,” or “cute,” is not a sign of weakness or inferiority, but an endearing trait that encourages harmony and communication — both valued in Japanese society.And so, if the need is for a soulmate, it’s better to have that cute look, be it a dog, cat or even a duck, said Jerry Wang, Executive Chairman of FF EAI Robotics Ecosystem, a U.S. company that offers more foreboding-looking four-legged patrol robots.“If you want some emotional attachment, you want a cute shape,” he said. The portfolios of the country’s youngest generation of investors keep getting fatter. Launched earlier this year, Trump accounts allow deposits of up to $5,000 per year for each child until the age of 18 and various billionaires have even thrown some money into the mix.

The SpaceX shares work a little differently in that the organization will transfer one share of its stock to active Trump accounts in December, according to Musk’s post. Nearly 70 million accounts have been created thus far, the White House reported last month, though that’s largely a result of a change by the Treasury to allow for automatic enrollment.

Industry observers note that musk’s matching donation will come later, he remarked on X, sometime after mid-June 2027. That’s when a 366-day lockup expires that he agreed to as part of the SpaceX initial public offering earlier this year.

It has been revealed that the Starbase, Texas-based company noted that Gwynne Shotwell, its president and chief operating officer, previously pledged with her husband to donate more than 2 million shares to Trump accounts. But there are strict eligibility requirements associated with those donations, which parents can check online.

Combined, the gifts from the company, Musk, and Shotwell could have a value of more than $18 billion given the stock’s current price and if all eligible Trump accounts have been claimed. These donations also do something that’s delving into fresh territory: They guarantee that potentially millions of Americans will become long-term shareholders of SpaceX.

But that could create a conundrum of sorts for parents as more and more money is likely to flow into these accounts from billionaires.

According to recent reports, the Treasury recently implemented new rules that allow companies and other donors to gift individual stocks to these accounts, while also limiting trading activity in them, as The Wall Street Journal reported. Children and their parents can neither pick nor reject stocks that are donated to a child’s account—and they can’t sell them for five years.

And yet, there’s free money on the line. If parents don’t claim an account on behalf of their kid, their kid misses out on a potentially lucrative portfolio. Despite the move to automatic enrollment, some manual steps are still required, which means parents need to claim an account by downloading an app from the Trump accounts website.

#161548. Sizing GPU Memory for a RAG Service: KV Cache, Context and Concurrency

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1136 w)
📖 Baca
Hardware & Chips ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Sitepoint ↗ Open Full Page

Sizing GPU Memory for a RAG Service: KV Cache, Context and Concurrency

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1136 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sitepoint

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Stay up to date with AI tools, model releases, and developer workflows that matter.
  • A retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) app is usually drawn as a language model plus a vector database.
  • This article shows how to estimate that limit before you deploy, with a short script you can run, and then covers what else in the pipeline can slow responses down.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Stay up to date with AI tools, model releases, and developer workflows that matter.

In a recent development, weekly. Free. One click to leave.

7 Day Free Trial. Cancel Anytime.

A retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) app is usually drawn as a language model plus a vector database. When it goes live, the part that fails first is rarely the retrieval. It is GPU memory on the generation model, because a model that loads fine for one request can run out of memory when several users send long questions at once.

This article shows how to estimate that limit before you deploy, with a short script you can run, and then covers what else in the pipeline can slow responses down.

It has been revealed that serving a model takes more than its weights. The GPU also holds:.

the key-value (KV) cache, which grows with the length of every active request.

activations and batching overhead.

memory used by the inference runtime itself.

SitePoint's guide to running a local LLM on 10GB of VRAM makes the same point for a single desktop GPU: the usable budget is the total VRAM minus overhead, and the KV cache grows with the context window, so the real model budget is smaller than the number on the box.

It has been revealed that for a RAG service, the KV cache matters even more. Retrieved passages are pasted into the prompt, so every request carries a long context, and every concurrent request holds its own cache.

In a recent development, the cache size per token depends on the model's architecture: two tensors (keys and values) for every layer, for every KV head. This script turns those numbers into a rough limit on concurrent requests:.

def kv_bytes_per_token(layers, kv_heads, head_dim, dtype_bytes=2):.

# Keys and values, for every layer, for one token.

return 2 *layers *kv_heads *head_dim *dtype_bytes.

def max_concurrent(vram_gb, weights_gb, ctx_tokens, per_token, reserve_gb=2.0):.

budget = (vram_gb - weights_gb - reserve_gb) * GIB.

return int(budget // (ctx_tokens * per_token)).

per_token = kv_bytes_per_token(32, 8, 128).

print(per_token // 1024, "KiB per token").

for ctx in (4096, 8192, 16384):.

n = max_concurrent(24, 16, ctx, per_token).

print(ctx, "tokens ->", n, "concurrent requests").

For a 24 GB GPU holding about 16 GB of fp16 weights with 2 GB kept in reserve, it prints:.

4096 tokens -> 12 concurrent requests.

8192 tokens -> 6 concurrent requests.

16384 tokens -> 3 concurrent requests.

The numbers are estimates. Real runtimes add their own overhead, and the architecture values come from the model's configuration file, so read them from the model you actually use. The pattern is what matters: doubling the context length halves the number of requests that fit. A RAG prompt that stuffs in ten retrieved chunks costs real capacity.

Industry observers note that serving runtimes do not simply crash when the cache is full. The vLLM documentation on optimization and tuning explains that when KV cache space is insufficient for all batched requests, the engine preempts some of them and recomputes them later, which can hurt end-to-end latency. Its suggested remedies include giving the cache more memory, reducing the number of concurrent sequences or batched tokens, or sharding the model across GPUs.

It has been revealed that so the symptom of undersizing is often not an error. It is slow, uneven responses under load. Test with realistic prompt lengths and several simultaneous consumers, not a single request.

According to recent reports, embedding and ingestion have a different profile from generation. Embedding is often lighter than serving a large language model, and some teams run it on CPU. Document parsing, chunking and tokenization also run on CPU, so a fast GPU cannot make up for a slow CPU upstream. SitePoint's tutorial on a local RAG system for private documents walks through chunking, embeddings, vector storage and reranking, and is a good map of which stages run where.

RAM: vector indexes, document loaders and caches all live in system memory, so large collections need more of it.

Recent findings suggest that storage: model files, indexes, logs and backups add up. Fast storage shortens model loading and re-indexing.

Network: if the vector database, application server and model server sit in different places, latency adds to every request.

Two layouts are common. A single instance runs everything and is simplest for prototypes and internal tools. Separated services put ingestion and retrieval on smaller machines and keep the GPU for generation, which scales better as traffic grows.

According to recent reports, memory estimates only hold if the GPU memory is really yours. On a shared or time-sliced GPU, other workloads can take memory and compute away from your service, which makes capacity hard to blueprint. Hosting providers describe this in different terms, such as passthrough, vGPU, MIG and time-slicing. For a view of how one GPU hosting provider explains those allocation methods, GPU Mart's GPU virtualization guide compares them. It is a hosting tech giant's page, so confirm any provider's claims about isolation and performance with your own load test.

Whatever provider you choose, ask these questions:.

Is the physical GPU assigned to you exclusively, or partitioned or time-sliced?

Do you have root access to install your own drivers, CUDA libraries and containers?

Which minimum commitments, regions and support terms apply?

In a recent development, A small stack can run as a handful of containers: an API service for request handling and prompt assembly, an ingestion worker, a vector database and a model server. Keeping them separate lets you monitor each one's memory and CPU use and move the heavy one to bigger hardware without rewriting the rest.

It has been revealed that for a service that stays up all month, a fixed monthly term is easier to forecast than hourly capacity. Hourly capacity suits testing quantization settings or processing a one-off document batch.

Is GPU memory always the bottleneck for RAG?

Not always. Generation usually hits memory first, but slow parsing, a small CPU or a distant vector database can dominate response time.

Does quantization solve the memory problem?

In a recent development, it shrinks the weights, but the KV cache still grows with context length and concurrency. Test with your real prompt sizes.

Should embeddings run on the GPU?

It depends on volume. Small workloads can run on CPU, while a large ingestion job may benefit from a GPU for a limited time.

Size a RAG service for the worst realistic moment, not the single-request demo. Estimate the KV cache from the model's architecture, remember that long retrieved contexts reduce how many requests fit, watch for preemption under load, keep CPU, RAM, storage and network in the plan, and find out whether the GPU is exclusive or shared. The script above is small, but it turns a vague worry about memory into numbers you can check.

This lightweight gaming mouse also features five programmable buttons and up to a 4,000 Hz wireless polling rate, and it's right now on sale at Best Buy for $79.99 — $40 off its MSRP of $119.99.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that password managers are the safest way short of secret sticky notes to keep track of the hundreds of logins in your life, but even they don’t have perfect security.
  • Password managers are the safest way short of secret sticky notes to keep track of the hundreds of logins in your life, but even they don’t have perfect security.
  • Industry observers note that popular Password manager 1Password disclosed this week that hackers breached its systems this month and accessed the software’s source code.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that password managers are the safest way short of secret sticky notes to keep track of the hundreds of logins in your life, but even they don’t have perfect security. Popular Password manager 1Password disclosed this week that hackers breached its systems this month and accessed the software’s source code. While no breach is good news, the attackers were not able to access 1Password users’ most sensitive data, including their passwords, secret keys, and information stored in user vaults. “At no time were customer vault contents accessed by, or available to, the attacker,” the organization emphasized in a blog post on the incident. The security of the software maker’s apps and browser extensions was also not affected by the breach. The attackers were able to burrow into 1Password’s system after gaining access to an employee’s corporate GitHub account. By pushing malicious code into its backend systems, the attackers made off with administrative data on a subset of 1Password customers, including customer names, email addresses, and “non-secret internal metadata” about accounts. Anyone who uses 1Password doesn’t need to take extra steps right now, but they should be extra vigilant for phishing attempts in the future. That includes being skeptical of “unexpected emails, texts or calls that mention 1Password, invitations, or account recovery attempts,” according to the company. The password manager will never ask its customers for an account password or a secret key. In response, 1Password claims that it has disabled the compromised GitHub account, rotated and revoked exposed internal credentials, and brought in external cybersecurity experts to advise the software maker on its response, among other measures. Security for everybody The world of cybersecurity moves fast – and now that cycle is speeding up even in light of AI. Security companies are leveraging artificial intelligence to detect threats at the same time that malicious actors are putting it to work cracking into accounts at scale. 1Password CTO Nancy Wang described the unique challenges and opportunities the company faces in light of widespread AI adoption in a recent interview with Fast Company. While a sea of vibe-coded apps have introduced security holes human software makers would have caught, AI can also scan massive chunks of code for vulnerabilities. “AI’s been a mixed bag, just because that work has been so gnarly and technical,” Wang said. Aside from the millions of people who rely on 1Password, more than 200,000 businesses use the password manager to keep track of their credentials. That number includes nearly a third of the largest companies in the U.S., according to 1Password. Fast Company named the software maker to its 2025 list of Brands That Matter for its user-friendly approach to security. “1Password was built on the belief that security should be accessible to everyone,” 1Password CEO David Faugno said last year. “In an industry that too often leads with fear and complexity, we’ve built our foundation on trust, usability, and the human experience.”.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that thanksgiving may be over, but one of the holiday’s biggest traditions is still to come.
  • Thanksgiving may be over, but one of the holiday’s biggest traditions is still to come.
  • According to recent reports, for the first time in its history, the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade is taking place on a day other than Thanksgiving.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that thanksgiving may be over, but one of the holiday’s biggest traditions is still to come. For the first time in its history, the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade is taking place on a day other than Thanksgiving. On Wednesday, Macy’s, NBC, and New York City officials made the unprecedented decision to postpone the parade until Saturday, November 28, after forecasts called for dangerous winds, heavy rain, and coastal flooding. While the parade was canceled from 1942 through 1944 during World War II, weather has never before forced organizers to move the event to another day. The timing is particularly noteworthy given that this year marks the parade’s 100th edition, a milestone Macy’s is celebrating with an expanded lineup of balloons, floats, musical performances, and celebrity appearances. NBC aired a replay of the 2025 parade on Thanksgiving morning instead. The live celebration will take place Saturday, although the last-minute schedule change has forced some performers to adjust their prepares. Here’s what to expect from the rescheduled parade and how to watch it. Who is performing at the 2026 Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade? Savannah Guthrie, Hoda Kotb, and Al Roker are slated to return as hosts of NBC’s broadcast. The originally confirmed musical lineup includes RAYE, Teddy Swims, Megan Moroney, Natasha Bedingfield, Queen Latifah, Jimmy Fallon and The Roots, JoJo, Smash Mouth, and Keke Palmer, among others. A special Broadway performance featuring a 10-minute medley from nine musicals, including Hamilton, Wicked, and Rent, is still expected to take place. The Radio City Rockettes are also on the announced lineup. However, not everyone who planned to participate on Thursday will be able to stick around for Saturday. The University of Alabama’s Million Dollar Band, for instance, is returning home to perform at Saturday’s Iron Bowl football game. Macy’s Great American Marching Band is also unable to participate in the rescheduled event. Other groups have turned to crowdfunding to cover the unexpected cost of extending their stays in New York. A high school marching band from Pearland, Texas, raised $350,000 in less than 24 hours to enable more than 500 students and staff members to stay for the parade. How to watch the 2026 Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade The rescheduled parade will step off at 8:30 a.m. ET on Saturday, November 28, and is expected to conclude around noon. NBC will televise the parade, while cord-cutters can stream it on Peacock. A Spanish-language broadcast will also be available on Telemundo. Viewers with live TV streaming subscriptions that carry NBC, including YouTube TV, Hulu + Live TV, and Fubo, can also tune in. If you’d rather sleep in on Saturday morning, NBC is scheduled to air an encore presentation at 2 p.m. ET/PT.

Set to launch on December 8, Nothing has confirmed its mysterious AI product will be called “Ear (note),” and it’s an AI recorder with earbuds inside.

Update 11/25: Nothing has shared another image of Ear (note), showing how the case opens and the earbuds inside. The firm adds that the audio quality matches Nothing’s “best in-ear audio experience,” explaining:.

It has been revealed that ear (note) is a newly introduced approach to personal productivity, making it easy to transcribe, summarise and act on in-person conversations, calls, online meetings and thoughts – without requiring an additional device or new behaviours. At the same time, Ear (note) doesn’t compromise on audio, combining Hi-Res Audio and high-quality audio capture with AI that works in the background.

Sources indicate that introducing a latest form factor, this is also the most evolved version of Nothing’s transparent design language. Built around an aluminium case with squared edges and a cool metallic finish, Ear (note) introduces machined metal and brutalist forms into Nothing’s transparent design language. Clear windows are inspired by the contours of topographic maps, revealing depth and dimensionality within the case. The TALK button and a new RECORD button draw on the controls on a retro Walkman, both positioned to be easy to reach and to provide tactile feedback when activated.

Speaking to Bloomberg, Nothing has confirmed that its upcoming AI product is “Ear (note).” This builds on a pair of earbuds by turning the charging case into an AI-powered recorder.

The case has a “Talk” button, like Ear (3), which can be used to record your own voice, where a record button enables the ability to “record and transcribe conversations.” Ear (3a)’s ability to record audio from the earbuds will also carry over to Ear (note), giving the product the ability to record both conversations in person and over the phone.

Nothing is entering a crowded market here with products from Plaud, Amazon, and countless others already offering AI recording/transcribing products, but building in earbuds is indeed a unique selling point.

Industry observers note that nothing Ear (note) is launching on December 8, though pricing is unclear. Pei’s comments suggest a subscription will be used in some capacity.

Generating a single AI video clip is easy now. You send a prompt and get a few seconds of footage back. The trouble starts when the goal is three, five, or ten minutes of video where the same character looks the same in every scene, the style does not drift, and the captions line up with the picture.

Most guides stop at the clip. This one covers the part after it, treating a video as a small build pipeline: a storyboard that is data, prompts generated from that data, clips normalised and stitched with ffmpeg, and captions derived from the same source. If you want to wire a generation model into your own application first, SitePoint's guide to integrating generative video APIs into web applications covers the request and webhook side. If the finished video is headed to a YouTube channel, how to get a YouTube API key and use the Data API is a good starting point for the publishing side. Everything between those two is below.

Long-form AI video fails at the seams between clips, not inside them. Initiative for continuity before you generate anything.

A storyboard stored as JSON can be validated, versioned, diffed, and turned into prompts by code, which a pile of loose prompts cannot.

According to recent reports, repeat the full character description in every prompt. Models do not remember the previous clip.

Clips from different generations rarely share resolution, frame rate, or codec settings. Normalise them before joining.

Captions are cheapest when generated from the script and measured clip durations, not transcribed afterwards.

Sources indicate that current video models generate short clips, commonly a handful of seconds each. A longer video is therefore many clips, and every clip is an independent generation. The model has no memory of what the character wore in the previous one.

That produces three kinds of failure. The character drifts, so hair, clothing, or proportions change between scenes. The style drifts, so lighting and colour grade shift from cut to cut. And the technical specs drift, so one clip is 24 frames per second at one resolution and the next is something else. Each of these is fixable, but only if the project is organised so the fixes can be applied consistently.

Start with a structured storyboard instead of a document full of prompts. One file holds the style, a "character bible", and an ordered list of scenes.

"project": "rainy-day-lantern",.

"style": "soft watercolor picture book illustration, warm evening light, 16:9",.

"mira": "a nine year old girl with short curly black hair, a yellow raincoat and red rubber boots",.

"lantern": "a small round paper lantern with a gentle orange glow and a tiny smiling face".

"setting": "a narrow cobblestone street in light rain",.

"action": "walks slowly past closed shops, looking up at the sky",.

"camera": "slow push in from a medium shot",.

"narration": "It had rained all afternoon, and the street was quiet.".

"characters": ["mira", "lantern"],.

"setting": "under a bakery awning",.

"action": "finds the lantern glowing on a wooden crate and kneels beside it",.

"camera": "static medium close up",.

"narration": "Then she noticed something glowing under the awning.".

Recent findings suggest that because it is data, a script can check it before you spend any generation credits. Two checks pay for themselves rapidly: every character named in a scene must exist in the bible, and no scene may be longer than the clip limit of the model you use.

const known = new Set(Object.keys(board.characters));.

for (const scene of board.scenes) {.

for (const name of scene.characters) {.

errors.push${scene.id}: unknown character "${name}");.

if (scene.duration > MAX_CLIP_SECONDS) {.

${scene.id}: ${scene.duration}s is over the ${MAX_CLIP_SECONDS}s clip limit, split it into shots.

According to recent reports, treat MAX_CLIP_SECONDS as a setting. Limits differ between models and change over time, so check the one you are using rather than trusting the number in this example.

Never write the per-scene prompt by hand. Generate it, so the style line and the character descriptions are identical every time.

Industry observers note that the character description appears word for word in every scene that includes that character. This is the single most effective consistency tactic that needs no special tooling. Changing a detail, say the colour of the boots, becomes one edit in the bible instead of a search through twenty prompts, and the diff highlights exactly what changed between versions.

Put the style line first and keep it identical across all scenes.

Describe one action per clip. Two sequential actions in one prompt often produce a blend of both.

Recent findings suggest that keep camera directions simple. A single move per clip is more reliable than a combination.

Industry observers note that avoid naming real people, brands, or existing characters in prompts. Beyond the rights problem, it makes results harder to reproduce.

Clips from separate generations often disagree on resolution, frame rate, pixel format, or codec parameters. Joining them directly can produce stutters, green frames, or an outright error. Convert every clip to one agreed format first.

-vf "scale=1280:720:force_original_aspect_ratio=decrease,pad=1280:720:(ow-iw)/2:(oh-ih)/2,fps=24,format=yuv420p" \.

-an -c:v libx264 -crf 18 "norm/$(basename "$f")".

According to recent reports, the filter scales each clip to fit a 1280 by 720 frame, adds padding if the aspect ratio differs, sets 24 frames per second, and forces a widely compatible pixel format. The -an flag drops any audio the model generated, since narration will be added as one track later. Name clips with zero padded numbers such as s01.mp4 and s02.mp4, so a shell glob sorts them in story order.

Once every file shares the same parameters, the concat demuxer can join them without re-encoding:.

for f in norm/*.mp4; do echo "file '$PWD/$f'"; done > list.txt.

ffmpeg -y -f concat -safe 0 -i list.txt -c copy stitched.mp4.

Industry observers note that hard cuts are the safe default. Crossfades are possible with ffmpeg's xfade filter, but they require careful offset arithmetic and a re-encode, so add them only when a cut genuinely looks wrong.

According to recent reports, captions are easiest when they come from the script, not from a speech recognition pass over the finished video. The storyboard already holds the narration text and each scene's length, so an SRT file is a few lines of code. Use measured durations rather than planned ones, because a generated clip is often a little shorter or longer than requested.

return Number(out.toString().trim());.

const ms = Math.round(totalSeconds * 1000);.

const h = String(Math.floor(ms / 3600000)).padStart(2, '0');.

const m = String(Math.floor((ms % 3600000) / 60000)).padStart(2, '0');.

const s = String(Math.floor((ms % 60000) / 1000)).padStart(2, '0');.

const rest = String(ms % 1000).padStart(3, '0');.

Recent findings suggest that revision each scene's duration from measureSeconds on the normalised clip before calling buildSrt. If a narration line is long, split it across two caption blocks so it stays readable. Then combine picture, voiceover, and captions in one final step:.

ffmpeg -y -i stitched.mp4 -i narration.mp3 -i captions.srt \.

-c:v copy -c:a aac -c:s mov_text -shortest final.mp4.

Soft captions like these can be switched off by the viewer and read by assistive technology, which is better than burning text into the picture. Keep the .srt file as well, since most platforms accept it as a separate upload.

Everything above is a good fit when you need repeatability: many videos from templates, versioned storyboards, automated publishing, or tight control over the model. The price is that you own the glue code, the ffmpeg settings, and the failures.

For one off projects, or when the people making the video are not developers, a managed platform is often the more sensible choice. Tools such as magiclight.ai bundle story to video generation, character handling, voice, and an editor in one interface, and advertise videos of up to 50 minutes. Check the specifics yourself, because claims like that are marketing, and results depend on your content. One point matters for developers in particular: if you need to automate generation from your own code, confirm that the platform you pick offers an API or export route before you build a workflow around it. A tool with a good editor and no programmatic access suits a different job than the pipeline in this article.

According to recent reports, A short manual pass catches what automation does not. Watch the whole video once at normal speed, looking only at continuity. Read the captions against the audio. Check that no real person's likeness, brand mark, or protected character slipped into the footage. Finally, check the disclosure rules of the platform you publish on, since many now ask creators to label realistic synthetic media, and the rules change.

The model is only one component of a long-form AI video. The reliability comes from the structure around it: a validated storyboard, prompts generated from it, clips forced into one format, and captions derived from measured data. Each of those is ordinary software engineering, and none of it depends on which generation model you choose, so the pipeline survives when the model changes.

In a recent development, start with a two minute video and four or five scenes. Fix the seams there before scaling up, because every continuity problem you find at that size is one you will not have to hunt for in a ten minute project.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Following its short-lived Galaxy Z TriFold, Samsung appears to have a sequel on the way that’s set to arrive in the Galaxy Z Fold 9 lineup.

The Galaxy Z TriFold introduced a few months after the Galaxy Z Fold 7, carrying the codename “Q7m.” GalaxyClub now reports that “Q9m” has surfaced, implying that Galaxy Z TriFold 2 will be based on the Galaxy Z Fold 9 series.

That tells us a couple of things.

Recent findings suggest that for one, don’t expect a latest TriFold to arrive in the same schedule as the first one. The original Galaxy Z TriFold launched in late 2025 before expanding to other regions in early 2026. While it’s abundantly clear we’re not getting a new model before the year lets out, this codename effectively rules out a release before the Galaxy Z Fold 9 series launches which, assuming it follows the usual schedule, won’t happen until around July.

This also tells us that the Galaxy Z TriFold 2 will be based on the Galaxy Z Fold 9 series, likely including the latest chipset and Samsung’s Android 18 build.

There’s no guarantee yet about when the next TriFold might debut, how much it might cost, or where it might launch. GalaxyClub notes that the codename subtly suggests there’s no EU release in the plans, but it can’t be completely ruled out either.

Whatever happens with Galaxy Z TriFold 2, let’s just hope it lasts longer than the original.

#161534. How to Finance Your Business’s Next Stage of Growth
